sections: What does it mean to flatten a PDF?

Flattening merges interactive or layered parts of a PDF – fillable form fields, check boxes, drop-downs, comments, stamps and drawings – into the page itself. The document looks the same, but those elements stop being separate editable objects. A flattened form shows the answers as ordinary page content that cannot be changed by clicking into a field, and it prints and displays the same in every viewer.

People flatten PDFs before sending completed applications, contracts or tax forms, before archiving, when a portal rejects files with form fields, and when filled-in answers disappear or look different in another app.

sections: How to flatten a PDF so it cannot be edited

After flattening, form answers can no longer be changed by typing into fields. Bear in mind that any PDF can still be modified with an editor – flattening prevents accidental and casual changes, not determined tampering. For stronger protection, add a password with editing disabled using [Protect PDF](/protect-pdf/), and for proof of integrity use a certificate-based digital signature.
Does flattening decrease quality?

*Form fields* mode does not touch the rest of the page, so quality is identical. *All content* mode renders pages at about 144 dpi with high JPEG quality, which looks sharp on screen and in normal printing, but text becomes part of an image and the file can grow for text-heavy documents. Use it when appearance matters more than size or searchability.
Flattening a large PDF

Form-field flattening is quick even for long documents. All-content mode renders every page, so a 200-page file takes longer and the output may be larger; you can run [Compress PDF](/compress-pdf/) afterwards. A progress counter shows which page is being processed.
Why answers vanish without flattening

Some viewers, mobile apps and print drivers do not display form field values correctly, especially when fields use custom fonts or scripts. The person receiving your form may see empty boxes. Flattening draws the values into the page so everyone sees the same thing.
Flatten PDF online vs desktop software

Desktop editors can flatten through print-to-PDF or preflight tools, often in paid versions. Online services usually require uploading your completed form – including personal details like ID numbers and addresses. This tool flattens on your device, for free.

sections: Worked example

A completed job application form has fields that look different on every viewer and can be changed by anyone. Drop it here, flatten, and send the result: the answers now look identical everywhere, print reliably, and can no longer be edited by mistake. Keep your fillable original in case you need to update an answer later.
When not to flatten

Do not flatten a form that someone else still needs to fill in, or a document you will edit again. Flattening is a final step, like printing to paper: do it on a copy, just before sending or archiving.
Privacy

Everything happens inside your browser tab with pdf-lib and PDF.js. The PDF is read from your disk into memory, processed there and saved straight back to your device. It is never uploaded, stored or logged, and the tool keeps working offline once the page has loaded – which makes it suitable for contracts, medical records, HR files, bank statements and anything else you would not e-mail to a stranger.
